paper_title: New constraints on light Axion-Like Particles using Chandra Transmission Grating Spectroscopy of the powerful cluster-hosted quasar H1821+643
suggested_experiment_name: Chandra Transmission Grating Spectroscopy of H1821+643
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling
notes: Paper presents new exclusion limits on axion-like particle (ALP) coupling to photons using Chandra transmission grating spectroscopy of quasar H1821+643 in cool-core cluster CL1821+643. At 99.7% credibility (3σ), the paper excludes g_aγ > 6.3×10^-13 GeV^-1 for most ALP masses m_a < 10^-12 eV. At 95.5% credibility (2σ), the limit is g_aγ > 5.0×10^-13 GeV^-1 in the same mass range. The constraint is mass-independent (flat) over the range m_a < 10^-12 eV, so encoded as a horizontal line from 10^-19 eV to 10^-12 eV. The analysis uses 571 ks combined HETG/LETG observations and assumes thermal-to-magnetic pressure ratio β=100 up to virial radius. The limit is derived from absence of spectral distortions due to photon-ALP oscillations in the magnetized intracluster medium. This represents the tightest constraint to date on light ALPs with log(m_a/eV) < -12.0, marginally improving upon Reynolds et al.
